summary: Kosei Ishii is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda University (~1974–1984). He held posts at Waseda, Komazawa Junior College, Nagoya University, and served as professor at Komazawa University (~2005–2016).

Kosei Mizutani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Bukkyo University (~1948–1952). He served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (~1960–1968) and later as president (~1979–1987).

Kosei Tada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1966). He held a post at Taisho University (~1974–2009) and served as director of the Society for Buddhist Cultural Studies (attested 2004).
Koshin Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a researcher (attested 1995–1998).

Koshiro Tamaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1943). He held posts at Toyo University, Tohoku University, Nihon University, and the University of Tokyo.

Kosho Kawamura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1948–1952) under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura. He worked at Toyo University (~1957–1994).
Kosho Uchiyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Waseda University (~1934–1941) and under Kodo Sawaki (~1941–1965), whom he succeeded.

Kotatsu Fujita was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, under supervisors Shoson Miyamoto and Hajime Nakamura, and at Harvard University. He was a professor at Hokkaido University (~1968–1991).
Koun Kajiyoshi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and held an academic post at Taisho University.

Koun Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the First Higher School (~1926–1929) and Tokyo Imperial University (~1929–1932). He held a post at NOF Corporation (~1941–1967) and succeeded Hakuun Yasutani.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi and held a post as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1995).

Koyu Tamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed his master's at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1956). He held posts at Nishogakusha University and Toyo University (~1974–2002), where he was a professor.

Krishna Kanta Handiqui was an Indologist who studied at Cotton University, Sanskrit College and University, University of Calcutta, and University of Oxford. He served as Principal at Jagannath Barooah College (~1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor at Gauhati University (~1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied at Hare School and Presidency University, Kolkata. He held posts at Hare School (~1829–1832) and Bishop's College, Kolkata (attested 1869–1870).

Krishnanath Chatterjee is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amareshwar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Colby College and Harvard University under supervisors and mentors including Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey, later teaching at Harvard, Brown, and Bard.

Kristina Myrvold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Lund University, where she also worked as an editor, and later served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

Kristofer Schipper was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied in Paris at the Faculty of Arts, EPHE, and ENLOV. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1970) and Leiden University (~1993–1999).

Krisztina Teleki is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA in Tibetan and Mongolian majors (~1997–2009) and served as a research fellow (~2009) at Eötvös Loránd University.
